events.title: Battle of Stirling Bridge
events.description: Scottish forces led by William Wallace and Andrew Moray defeated a larger English army at the River Forth near Stirling. A narrow wooden bridge kept the English from using their numbers, and the Scots struck as part of the army was crossing.
events.significance: The victory was a major early triumph in the First War of Scottish Independence. It made Wallace a national hero and showed that a smaller force could beat England's heavy cavalry.

events.title: Construction Begins on the Pentagon
events.description: Ground was broken in Arlington, Virginia, for the new headquarters of the United States War Department. The building was designed to bring scattered offices together under one roof as World War II spread.
events.significance: The Pentagon became one of the world's best-known government buildings and a lasting symbol of American military power. It was completed in about sixteen months.

events.title: Military Coup in Chile
events.description: Chilean armed forces led by General Augusto Pinochet overthrew President Salvador Allende. Allende died during the attack on the presidential palace in Santiago.
events.significance: The coup ended Chile's long democratic tradition and began a 17-year military dictatorship. It was marked by human rights abuses and sweeping free-market reforms.

events.title: September 11 Attacks
events.description: Terrorists from al-Qaeda hijacked four airliners in the United States. Two were flown into the World Trade Center towers in New York City, one into the Pentagon, and one crashed in a field in Pennsylvania after passengers resisted. Nearly 3,000 people died.
events.significance: These were the deadliest terrorist attacks in history. They led to the US-led war in Afghanistan, major changes in global security and intelligence policy, and the wider war on terror.
